note.explanation: A temporary magnet acts as a magnet while it is in a magnetic field, but loses its magnetism when that field disappears. A permanent magnet keeps its magnetic properties. Soft iron is commonly used for temporary magnets; steel and special alloys can be used for permanent magnets.
examples: An iron nail attracted to a magnet can temporarily attract another nail.
Cobalt, alnico and ferrite are examples of materials used for permanent magnets.
note.checkAnswer: Temporary magnets lose their magnetic properties when the magnetic field vanishes; permanent magnets retain their magnetic properties.
note.simple: Temporary means the magnetism does not last once the outside magnetic field is gone. Permanent means the magnetism remains.
note.checkQuestion: What happens to a chain of iron nails when it is pulled away from the bar magnet?
note.title: Temporary and Permanent Magnets
steps: Bring an iron nail into contact with a bar magnet.
The nail becomes a temporary magnet and can attract another iron nail.
Remove the chain from the bar magnet.
The iron-nail chain immediately collapses, showing that its induced magnetism was temporary.
note.answer: The chain immediately collapses because the magnetism induced in the iron nails is temporary.

example.question: What does the activity with a bar magnet and chains of iron and steel nails show?
example.answer: The magnetism induced in iron nails is temporary, while that induced in steel nails is permanent.

explain.title: Temporary magnets
explain.body: Temporary magnets are the magnets that work in the presence of a magnetic field of permanent magnets. Once the magnetic field vanishes, they lose their magnetic properties.

explain.title: Materials for temporary magnets
explain.body: Usually, soft iron is used to make temporary magnets. Paper clips, office pins and iron nails can easily be made temporary magnets. Electromagnets are also good examples of temporary magnets.

explain.title: Permanent magnets
explain.body: Permanent magnets retain their magnetic properties forever. These are either found in nature or artificially made by placing objects made of steel and some special alloys in a strong magnetic field for a sufficient time.

explain.title: Examples and the nail-chain activity
explain.body: Cobalt, alnico and ferrite are examples of permanent magnetic materials. In the activity, the iron-nail chain immediately collapses when removed, while steel nails remain attached to each other for some time. This shows that magnetism induced in iron is temporary while that in steel is permanent.

mistakes: Do not confuse temporary magnets, which lose their magnetic properties when the field vanishes, with permanent magnets, which retain them.
Do not write that all iron is permanently magnetised; the activity shows that magnetism induced in the iron nails is temporary.
Do not claim that steel nails immediately collapse in the activity; they remain attached to each other for some time.
When giving examples, do not label soft iron as a usual material for permanent magnets; the textbook gives it as the usual material for temporary magnets.
